1. FROM MY DESK
The 10-year Treasury yield touching 5% underscores a new wild card in sovereign debt: hedge funds.
With traditional pension funds stepping back, fast-twitch traders have seized a record 7% of the Treasury market, where $1.2 trillion of securities change hands every day.

Hedge funds entered the year holding about $2 trillion in Treasurys. Some of those holdings stem from "basis trades," where funds borrow money to capitalize on bond-futures price gaps and amplify gains.

That shift has the New York Fed quietly asking investors whether new risks are creeping into U.S. Treasurys. In a market strained by inflation and ballooning debt, these active players leave little margin for error.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Driscoll's gave China its blueberries-then China swiped the secret to growing them.

About 15 years ago, executives from U.S. fruit grower Driscoll's went to China with a goal of turning blueberries into that country's next big food trend. Since then, Driscoll's has become the latest U.S. firm to hit the buzz saw of Chinese competition, reports Jon Emont. As tales of blueberry fortunes spread, Chinese entrepreneurs rapidly built farms of their own. They also swiped the company's patent-protected varieties, a Chinese court has ruled. For just about everyone in the blueberry business, though, it has been a knife fight, plagued by intellectual-property theft and tanking profits.

9. AND FINALLY...
Welcome to the school where students do farmwork and chores-and pay $40,000 a semester.

At the semesterlong Mountain School program, families pay $40,000 for their teens to do chores on a farm in rural Vermont. Three times most days, groups of high-school juniors scrape, scrub and stow kitchenware and cutlery. They're responsible for "commons work"-cleaning classrooms, prepping vegetables and checking irrigation systems. They also harvest corn, herd sheep, care for cows and chop wood. Some students and alums consider the Mountain School a secret path to top universities. Other families are seeking a wider perspective beyond traditional schooling and a rare reprieve from technology.
